card.title: Convex lens ray diagram: locating the real image

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Two rays fix the image of any object: the ray parallel to the principal axis leaves through the far focus F', and the ray through the optical centre passes straight on. Where they cross is where the image forms.

figure.caption: Object beyond F: the parallel ray and the central ray cross where the real, inverted image forms.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: 1/v − 1/u = 1/f;  m = v/u = h'/h;  P = 1/f in dioptres

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Thin lens, paraxial rays, and the Cartesian sign convention — distances measured against the incident light are negative.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Object at 2F gives an image at 2F, same size and inverted; an object inside F gives a virtual, upright, magnified image on the same side.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: f = 20 cm, u = −30 cm → 1/v = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60 → v = +60 cm and m = v/u = −2, an inverted image twice as large.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The construction ignores lens thickness and aberrations, so it predicts a sharp image where a real lens gives a blurred one.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Parallel ray refracted through F'; central ray undeviated; similar triangles give h'/h = v/u and the thin-lens relation 1/v − 1/u = 1/f

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Draw the parallel ray first and the central ray second — their crossing IS the image; sketch before you calculate.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Draw a ray diagram for a convex lens with the object beyond 2F, locate the image and state its nature.
